title: Stacks, Queues, Monotonic Deque & Priority Queue (Depth Pass)
relevance: High (contest-form stack/deque/heap greeds beyond LC NGE / sliding-window max / top-K; trains CF-style observation on the same DS).
company_notes: Serve customers from preferred then cheapest stock — Lunar New Year / multi-queue inventory simulation. k workers on the most non-overlapping intervals — Movie Festival II / Meeting Rooms II with k rooms. Running k-th largest in a stream / prefix — ABC234 D; top-K heap interview staple. For every window length, max of the window minimum — Mike and Feet; histogram / contribution interviews in CF clothing.

phases.goal: Spot depth-pass asks that hide lex-min deque greeds, capped sort+heap loot, stack cancel, nearest-smaller ranges, or lazy PQ offsets behind contest wording.

must_hit.point: Statements hide the same LIFO / FIFO / extremum-in-window ideas behind lex-minimization with a deque, capped “who can take whom” heaps after a sort, cancel-pairs on a stack, nearest-smaller ranges that feed histogram / contribution formulas, or regret-style PQ undos.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names at least one of those hidden wrappers instead of plain NGE / sliding-window max / top-K.

must_hit.point: Recognize it when order of processing is forced (left→right, by power, by deadline), when each index needs its nearest stricter neighbor, when a sliding window only needs min/max (not k-th), or when a global add on all heap keys can be deferred as a lazy offset.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites forced processing order, nearest stricter neighbor, window min/max only, or lazy global heap add as the cue.

must_hit.point: OA-flavoured inventory / k-resource interval / streaming k-th / max-of-window-minimum wording maps to Lunar New Year, Movie Festival II, ABC234 D, and Mike and Feet-style contribution.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties preferred-then-cheapest stock, k non-overlapping watchers, prefix k-th largest, or max of minima per length to this DS family.

probes: What in the statement says this is lex-min with a deque, capped loot after a sort, stack cancel, nearest-smaller ranges, or a lazy heap offset rather than plain NGE / window max / top-K?
Is processing order forced, does each index need a nearest stricter neighbor, does the window only need min/max, or can a global heap add be deferred?

hints.1: Look past stack/queue/heap keywords — ask what contest wrapper is hiding the template.
hints.2: Forced order, nearest stricter neighbor, window min/max (not k-th), or global +Δ deferred as lazy offset are the depth signals.
hints.3: Say: lex-min / cancel-pairs / capped sort+heap / nearest-smaller→histogram / lazy PQ offset; OA cousins are preferred-then-cheapest, k rooms, streaming k-th, max of window minima.

phases.goal: Pick the right depth model from the technique notes: L/R nearest-smaller, lazy PQ offset, size-k heap, capped loot, stack cancel, mono deque DP, or merge/frequency PQ.

must_hit.point: Nearest-smaller/greater on both sides gives, for each i, the maximal segment where a[i] is the min (or max); then push answers by segment length (Mike and Feet) or check prefix conditions inside that range (Max GEQ Sum).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States L/R bounds define the maximal min/max segment, then length answers or prefix checks inside the range.

must_hit.point: Lazy heap offset: store value − global_add in the PQ; type-2 “add X to all” only bumps global_add (ABC212 D).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Stores shifted keys and bumps a global add instead of touching every entry.

must_hit.point: Size-k heap for k-th largest in a growing prefix: min-heap of size k; top is the answer after each insert (ABC234 D).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maintains a size-k min-heap whose top is the streaming k-th largest.

must_hit.point: Capped loot heap: process entities sorted by strength; maintain a size-k multiset of taken values, evicting the minimum when over capacity (Knights).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts by power and keeps a capacity-k multiset, dropping the minimum when full.

must_hit.point: Histogram / Skyscrapers: after L/R bounds, ans[i] is often a prefix contribution from the left stack plus a suffix from the right — compute both passes, then pick the best peak.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Runs left and right contribution passes from L/R bounds and picks the best peak.

must_hit.point: Mono deque DP: window min of dp[j] (or of a[j]) over a sliding feasible interval turns O(nk) into O(n) (Strip / Cashback-family).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Replaces an O(nk) sliding min transition with a mono deque for O(n).

must_hit.point: Merge-equals / frequency PQ: always combine the current minimum key (or highest freq); use map/multiset so the next candidate is O(log n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Always merges the current min key or highest freq via map/multiset for O(log n) next picks.

probes: Given nearest-smaller L/R bounds, do you answer by segment length, prefix checks inside the range, or left+right contribution peaks?
When do you use a lazy PQ offset, a size-k min-heap, a capped loot multiset, or a mono deque DP window?

hints.1: Match the ask to one technique-note template, not generic stack/heap.
hints.2: L/R segment → length or prefix check or both-side contributions; lazy add; size-k min-heap; capped multiset; mono deque for sliding DP min; map/multiset merges.
hints.3: Say: Mike and Feet / Max GEQ Sum from L/R; Skyscrapers left+right peaks; ABC212 D store value−add; ABC234 D size-k min-heap; Knights capacity-k multiset; Strip O(nk)→O(n) mono deque; Merge Equals / frequency via map/multiset.

phases.goal: Encode L/R mono-stack passes, length-indexed suffix-max, mono deque window ops, size-k / lazy PQ templates, lex stack+suffix mins, and multiset lower_bound assignment.

must_hit.point: Write nearest-smaller/greater L/R arrays in one left-to-right and one right-to-left mono-stack pass.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches two mono-stack sweeps to fill L and R nearest-stricter neighbors.

must_hit.point: Convert L/R bounds into length-indexed answers (ans[len]=max(ans[len],a[i])) then suffix-max sweep.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Fills ans by segment length from L/R then sweeps suffix maxima.

must_hit.point: Maintain a monotonic deque of indices for window min/max; expire from the front, pop dominated from the back.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Expires stale front indices and pops dominated candidates from the back.

must_hit.point: Lazy global offset on a PQ: store x−add, bump add for “add to all keys” queries; size-k heap / capped multiset for streaming k-th and top-k loot while scanning.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Implements store x−add plus capacity-k heap/multiset templates.

must_hit.point: Stack greedy for lex-smallest output: pop while safe w.r.t. a precomputed suffix minimum (Minimal String); multiset lower_bound / upper_bound for modular or interval assignment (Minimum Array, Movie Festival II).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Pops while top ≤ remaining suffix minimum, or assigns via multiset bound queries.

probes: How do you build L/R nearest-smaller arrays and turn them into length-indexed answers?
How do you maintain a mono deque window, a lazy PQ offset, or a lex stack with suffix minima?

hints.1: Implementation is checklist bookkeeping: two mono-stack passes, deque front/back, lazy add, suffix mins.
hints.2: L then R mono-stack; ans[len] then suffix-max; expire front / pop back; store x−add; pop while ≤ suffix min; multiset lower_bound.
hints.3: Say: LTR+RTL mono-stack for L/R; ans[len]=max then suffix-max; deque indices with front expire and back pop; PQ stores x−add; Minimal String pops vs suffix min; Movie Festival II / Minimum Array use multiset bounds.

phases.goal: Justify O(n) mono deque / window minima and O(log n) map/multiset candidates; refuse O(nk) sliding DP mins and per-key global adds.

must_hit.point: Mono deque DP over a sliding feasible window turns an O(nk) min-of-prior-states transition into O(n) (Strip / Cashback-family).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(nk)→O(n) via mono deque on the sliding DP window.

must_hit.point: Canonical sliding-window minima with a monotonic deque run in O(n); when the DP transition is min over a sliding feasible window, reach for a mono deque — not a segtree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites O(n) window minima and prefers mono deque over segtree for that sliding min.

must_hit.point: Merge-equals / frequency PQ with map/multiset keeps the next candidate O(log n) instead of scanning all keys.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names O(log n) next-candidate cost from map/multiset.

probes: Why does a sliding feasible min of prior DP states go from O(nk) to O(n) with a mono deque?
When is map/multiset O(log n) the right merge structure, and when is a segtree the wrong tool for window min DP?

hints.1: Complexity fails are O(nk) sliding mins or touching every heap key / scanning for the next merge.
hints.2: Mono deque → O(n) window/DP min; map/multiset → O(log n) next candidate; not segtree for plain sliding min DP.
hints.3: Cite Strip/Cashback O(nk)→O(n); CSES-style O(n) window minima; Merge Equals / frequency via map/multiset O(log n); checklist says mono deque not segtree.

phases.goal: Catch depth-pass failure modes: segtree overkill, eager global heap updates, missing suffix-max after L/R, and unsafe lex pops.

must_hit.point: Using a segtree when the DP transition is min over a sliding feasible window of prior states — the checklist says reach for a mono deque.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects segtree for that sliding min and names mono deque.

must_hit.point: Implementing “add X to all” by touching every PQ key instead of storing value − global_add and bumping global_add (ABC212 D).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags per-key updates and describes the lazy offset.

must_hit.point: Stopping after L/R nearest-smaller bounds without converting to length-indexed ans[len]=max(ans[len],a[i]) and a suffix-max sweep (Mike and Feet-style).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires the length-index fill plus suffix-max after L/R.

must_hit.point: Lex-smallest stack greedy that pops without consulting a precomputed suffix minimum (Minimal String requires pop while top ≤ remaining minimum).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires the suffix-minimum safety check before each pop to output.

must_hit.point: Mono deque bugs: forgetting to expire from the front or to pop dominated indices from the back when maintaining window min/max.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions both front expiry and back dominance pops.

probes: What’s wrong with answering sliding DP window min with a segtree, or global heap adds by updating every key?
Where do Mike and Feet-style and Minimal String solutions fail after the obvious stack pass?

hints.1: Depth bugs are skipping checklist bookkeeping after the obvious stack/heap.
hints.2: Mono deque not segtree; lazy offset not per-key add; L/R then ans[len]+suffix-max; pop only if ≤ suffix min; expire front and pop back.
hints.3: Say: sliding DP min → mono deque; ABC212 D → store value−add; Mike and Feet → length index then suffix-max; Minimal String → suffix min gate; window deque → front expire + back pop.

tradeoffs.topic: Mono deque vs segtree for sliding DP window min
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When the transition is min over a sliding feasible window of prior states (or of a[j]), a mono deque turns O(nk) into O(n); the checklist says not to reach for a segtree for that pattern (Strip / Cashback-family).

tradeoffs.topic: Lazy PQ offset vs updating every heap key
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For type-2 “add X to all”, store value − global_add in the PQ and only bump global_add (ABC212 D) instead of rewriting every key.

tradeoffs.topic: Size-k min-heap vs full resort for streaming k-th
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For k-th largest on a growing prefix, keep a min-heap of size k whose top is the answer after each insert (ABC234 D) rather than re-sorting the whole prefix.

tradeoffs.topic: Capped multiset loot vs unrestricted heap while scanning by power
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Process by strength and keep a size-k multiset of taken values, evicting the minimum when over capacity (Knights), instead of accumulating unlimited loot.

tradeoffs.topic: L/R nearest-smaller contribution vs recomputing per length or per peak
tradeoffs.strong_answer: One LTR and one RTL mono-stack build L/R; then either length-index + suffix-max (Mike and Feet), prefix checks inside the max-range (Max GEQ Sum), or left+right contribution passes picking the best peak (Skyscrapers).

tradeoffs.topic: Stack + suffix mins vs blind stack pops for lex-min strings
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For lex-smallest output, pop to the answer while top ≤ remaining suffix minimum (Minimal String); do not pop solely by local comparison without the suffix gate.

gotchas.trap: Answering sliding feasible-window DP min with a segment tree.
gotchas.correction: Use a monotonic deque of indices; that transition is O(n), not a segtree job.

gotchas.trap: Global “add X to all heap keys” by mutating every entry.
gotchas.correction: Store value − global_add and bump global_add only (ABC212 D).

gotchas.trap: Building L/R nearest-smaller arrays but never doing the length-index + suffix-max sweep.
gotchas.correction: Set ans[len]=max(ans[len],a[i]) from each maximal segment, then suffix-max for every length (Mike and Feet).

gotchas.trap: Lex stack that pops whenever the top looks large, without a suffix minimum.
gotchas.correction: Precompute suffix mins; pop to output only while top ≤ remaining minimum (Minimal String).

gotchas.trap: Mono deque that only inserts, never expires the front or pops dominated backs.
gotchas.correction: Expire indices that leave the window from the front; pop dominated candidates from the back.

gotchas.trap: Streaming k-th largest with an unbounded structure or full prefix sort each time.
gotchas.correction: Keep a min-heap of size k; after each insert the top is the k-th largest (ABC234 D).

gotchas.trap: Assigning intervals/resources without multiset lower_bound / upper_bound on free ends.
gotchas.correction: For k resources, assign each film to the latest free end ≤ start (Movie Festival II); similarly use multiset bounds for modular picks (Minimum Array).
